title.value: Sales per active household by week
Promotion share of sales by week

lines: Weeks 1–13 are the panel ramp-up: households were still joining (88 active in week 1, over 1,000 from week 14), so use sales per active household for trends. Weeks 1 and 102 cover only 5 and 6 days, so the trend charts leave out these partial weeks. Promotion share is recorded only for weeks 9–101 in the 115 stores with promotion data.

Associations, not causal effects: the retailer chooses what to promote. Mailer-week lift includes the price cut that usually comes with a mailer feature. Display lift is approximate, for the stores that have the display. Source: notebook 10.

title.value: Share of households and of spend

lines: Segments describe price-and-promotion behaviour, measured against shoppers buying the same categories in the same stores. "Expected" is what those shoppers show; the gap is the segment's own behaviour. Demographics are not shown: they cover only 801 heavier-shopping households. Source: notebook 20.

pages.displayName: How well the model would have targeted past campaigns

frame.title: Redemptions captured by targeting the top 20% (model)

lines: A back-test: each past campaign sent to its top X% of eligible households by out-of-fold score (scores from models that never saw that household). It predicts redemption, not extra sales: heavy coupon users may have bought anyway. Targeting a future campaign needs a scoring job (future work). Source: notebook 30.

frame.title: Checks passed and failed, latest run

lines: Silver keeps problem rows and flags them; only exact duplicate rows are dropped. "Modified" means a value was changed, for example a blank set to empty or two conflicting promotion records merged, and every change is logged with its reason. "Error" checks stop a run; "warning" checks are recorded only.
